chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
It is written in the Torah: 'O son of Adam! Be as you wish. Just as you pay back to you what you have paid out.'
The one who is pleased with Allah with little sustenance, Allah accepts from him the small amount of deeds.
And whoever is pleased with the little of the permissible, his expenditure becomes light, his earnings become pure, and he exits from the boundary of immorality.

key_terms.كَمَا تَدِينُ تُدَانُ: Just as you pay back, so shall you be paid back (reciprocity)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of being content with little sustenance and halal earnings?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) cites a *hadith qudsi*-like tradition from the Torah to illustrate the principle of *qada'* (divine recompense) based on one's spiritual state. This narration underscores the Shia emphasis on *rida* (contentment) not merely as passive acceptance, but as an active purification of wealth and deeds, linking material simplicity directly to moral integrity and divine acceptance.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Abdullah Bin Al Qasim, from Amro Bin Abu Al Miqdam,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘It is written in the Torah: “O son of Adam<sup>as</sup>! Become howsoever you desire to. Just as you sow, so shall you reap”!
The one who was pleased from Allah<sup>azwj</sup> with the little from the sustenance, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Accept the less deeds from him.
The one who was pleased with the less from the Permissible (means), his expenditure would be light, and his earnings would be pure, and he would be outside from the boundary of the immoralities’.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from his father from ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Qasim from ‘Amr ibn abu al-Miqdam from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
It is written in the Torah: ‘O sons of Adam, be as you like to be. You shall reap as you sow.
Whoever becomes happy with Allah for a little amount of sustenance, Allah will accept his little good deeds.
Whoever becomes happy with the little but lawful, his expenses become light, his earnings pure and he will be out of the limits (environments) of sins.’”
